key_insight: FREDI jointly optimizes fair wireless resource allocation and dual-threshold early-exit inference so secure edge intelligence can detect critical events efficiently without sacrificing user fairness.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical optimization blueprint for secure UE–edge–cloud systems, balancing latency, bandwidth, compute, and per-user fairness under event-triggered inference.
method: Dual-threshold early-exit CNN screening at the UE identifies critical events before offloading.
Proportional-fair optimization jointly selects UE–ES associations, bandwidth, power, and confidence thresholds.
Set-monotonicity and finite confidence-domain properties enable exact threshold search and certified resource allocation.
evidence_signal: Experiments with MobileNetV2 and ShuffleNetV2 show near-perfect UE fairness, aggregate utility close to a Sum-Utility benchmark, and Stage-A scaling from 6 to 144 UEs with median solving time below 0.1 s.
watch_item: The method’s certified optimization depends on exact confidence-domain discretization and mixed-integer exponential-cone solving, which may become challenging as network scale or model complexity increases.
paper_title: Proportional-Fair Resource Allocation and Dual-Threshold Early-Exit Inference for Secure Cooperative Multi-Layer Edge Intelligence
